summary.text: An 81-year-old man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, iron deficiency anemia, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, coronary artery disease treated with percutaneous coronary angioplasty and benign prostatic hyperplasia presented with progressively worsening shortness of breath 5 months after transfemoral TAVR with a 29 mm Medtronic Evolut PRO + valve. Examination documented a regular rhythm, 3/6 end-diastolic and mid-systolic murmurs and clear lungs.

Echocardiography showed normal biventricular function with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 68%, severe mitral stenosis and multiple prosthetic aortic paravalvular jets graded moderate or severe depending on the parameter. Angiography found only 1+ leak and CT showed under-expansion of the prosthesis as the cause. CMR phase contrast imaging gave a regurgitant fraction of 39% and regurgitant volume of 35 ml, most consistent with clinically and hemodynamically significant paravalvular leak.

Based on CMR evaluation and following Heart Team discussion, the patient underwent surgical explant of the TAVR, re-do aortic valve replacement with a 23 mm porcine tissue valve, mitral valve replacement with a 25 mm tissue valve and left atrial appendage ligation. This was followed by clinical improvement and no residual aortic regurgitation on follow-up echocardiograms.

article_limitations: Case text gives no calendar dates, hospital course, discharge, follow-up duration or medication doses; only relative timing (5 months after TAVR) is stated.
Modality for the vena contracta area, flow convergence and circumferential extent is not named in their own sentences; method fields are left empty (see ambiguity).
Abstract describes angiographic PVL as mild while the case text states 1+ PVL; kept as an ambiguity, not mapped.
Discussion sentences are literature review (cited studies) and are not patient facts.
Supplementary Videos 1-6 and the CARE checklist are reviewed in the supplement manifest; no clinical facts were taken from video pixels.
